title: No test holds a commented key in config.reference.yaml to the schema, so a key documented only as a comment can name nothing devbin reads
body:
## Problem

`lib/config.reference.yaml` documents some keys only as comments, because declaring them would change what a project does. The `release:` block documents eight that way: `remotes`, `notes.run`, `derived`, `ci.query`, `ci.wait`, `repo`, `object_wait` and `after`.

`documentation.bats` holds the reference in one direction only. Its 4th arm ("the annotated reference config parses and validates") reads live keys only, and its 6th ("every schema key appears in the annotated reference config") runs from the schema to the file. Nothing runs from a commented key to the schema. So a commented key the schema does not know, or a renamed key whose comment stays behind, passes. For `docs/configuration.md` the 7th and 8th arms hold both directions; the yaml has no counterpart to the 8th.

## Measured at dbce992

All eight are rows of `_DEVBIN_RELEASE_SCHEMA` (`lib/config:482`) today, so this is latent, not live. Found by dc on 2026-10-05; the arm numbering and the eight keys were checked by vc against the schema block itself.

## Fix

An arm that extracts every commented `key:` in the reference's documented blocks, with the dotted path its nesting gives it, and requires each to be a schema row. A non-empty floor stops it passing on an empty population.

## Done when

1. A commented key the schema does not know fails the arm, driven red by planting one in a copy of the reference.
2. The arm reads every commented key in the file and fails on an empty population.

## Resolution

Fixed at bd81574c. `tests/unit/documentation.bats` gains `reference_comment_keys`, which reads every key `lib/config.reference.yaml` documents only in a comment, at the dotted path its nesting gives it, and an arm that requires each to be a path the schema knows, a list key with its index. `schema_path_known` asks that question, and the configuration page's arm now asks it through the same helper.

A key commented out with others nests where uncommenting it would put it. A parent is known by where it stands, so the same path written as a leaf elsewhere is still read. A run of commented keys that opens further right, as the example in the `iex` option's comment does, is read from its own first line. A key-shaped line inside prose is prose. One at the edge of prose, one indented past any key it could nest under, and one spelled as no key is (a capital, a hyphen, or no space after the `#`) come back unplaced, and the check names each of them rather than letting it go unread.

Both arms floor the population at eight, so an empty extraction fails. The extractor's own arm compares its whole output on a fixture holding every placement rule. The check's arm plants two unknown keys and a key too deep to place in a copy of the reference, and requires exactly those three to be named. Driven red on the real reference: an unknown key commented into its release block fails the check, naming it, and a copy with no commented key fails both floors. Each of 17 mutants of the extractor and the check, and each of 9 plants in the real reference, turns its aimed arm red.

Declared limit, in the extractor's comment: a key commented out with prose directly above and below it reads as prose. No commented key in the reference is written that way.

The full suite over this patch with 0169 v1 and 0166 v1 applied beside it, neither of which touches this file: 2069 of 2069 ok and 0 not ok (seal 20261005-1157, .errors empty). This patch's arms source `lib/helpers`, which 0169 and 0166 both change, so the landing tree itself, main with this patch alone, also ran `documentation.bats` and the tree-scan files `helpers.bats`, `contract.bats`, `neutral.bats`, `readonlygit.bats` and `harness.bats`: 198 of 198 ok and 0 not ok (seals 20261005-1209 and 20261005-1211, .errors empty).
